text_snippet: LIVRO DIGITAL ACESSÍVEL NA PREVENÇÃO DA VIOLÊNCIA SEXUAL DAS CRIANÇAS SURDAS ACCESSIBLE DIGITAL BOOKS ON THE PREVENTION OF SEXUAL VIOLENCE LIBRO DIGITAL ACCESIBLE EN LA PREVENCIÓN DE LA VIOLENCIA SEXUAL EN NIÑOS SORDOS Deaf children face multiple barriers in accessing sexual education and violence prevention initiatives. An investigation of existing educational materials revealed a significant gap in accessibility for this population. This study, approved by the Research Ethics Committee of UNESPAR (Opinion No. 6,668,278), analyzed the approach to sexual violence prevention for deaf children in early childhood education and the early years of elementary school in Ivaiporã, Paraná, Brazil. The research adopted a qualitative and exploratory approach, based on a literature review and data collection procedures involving structured interviews. The participants consisted of four teachers (three hearing and one deaf) working in inclusive education settings and Deaf Resource Rooms. Data analysis resulted in the organization of eight emerging categories, addressing teacher training, comfort in discussing the topic, children's perceptions, and family communication. The findings revealed a lack of accessible educational materials and teachers' insecurity in addressing the subject. title: CONTRIBUIÇÕES DA TECNOLOGIA ASSISTIVA PARA BRINCADEIRAS ACESSÍVEIS ACCESSIBLE PLAY THROUGH ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY CONTRIBUCIONES DE LA TECNOLOGÍA ASISTIVA PARA EL JUEGO ACCESIBLE
text_snippet: CONTRIBUIÇÕES DA TECNOLOGIA ASSISTIVA PARA BRINCADEIRAS ACESSÍVEIS ACCESSIBLE PLAY THROUGH ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY CONTRIBUCIONES DE LA TECNOLOGÍA ASISTIVA PARA EL JUEGO ACCESIBLE This paper presents and discusses the use and appropriation of Assistive Technologies (AT) by children with disabilities aged 0 to 6 years. It is a qualitative, bibliographical research linked to a longitudinal study on user evaluation and the development of AT products. The central question involves how resources and services are being organized to promote the integral development of children with disabilities, relating them to existing public policies in Brazil aimed at the appropriation and use of AT in early childhood, in educational and leisure contexts. The objective is to investigate support services for the use and appropriation of AT for children in early childhood in Brazil, considering the political, social, and legal dimensions, relating them to educational and leisure contexts. The results highlight the scarcity of publications on the subject, reflecting the invisibility of this population in social contexts, despite the existence of interministerial and multidimensional public policies that should address them. text_snippet: TECNOLOGÍA ASISTIVA EDUCATIVA EDUCATIONAL ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY TECNOLOGIA ASSISTIVA EDUCACIONAL Educational Assistive Technology (EAT), as formulated by Study and Research Group on Education, Technologies, and Languages (GEPETeL), constitutes an emerging conceptual category that distinguishes itself from ET, AT, UD, and UDL. This article analyzes its origin, foundations, and hybrid nature, understanding it as an inclusive educational technology oriented toward teaching planning. Based on theoretical and bibliographic, without the participation of human subjects and without the collection of empirical data, which is why submission to the Research Ethics Committee was not required, in which research, we discuss the evolution of pedagogical resources, the limitations of approaches centered on individual adaptations, and the need for a framework that articulates accessibility, pedagogical mediation, and human variability. We argue that EAT is not defined by the artifact itself, but by a universalist pedagogical intentionality that allows the same resource to function as AT for some students and as ET for others, without promoting segregation. text_snippet: IMPLEMENTAÇÃO DE TECNOLOGIA ASSISTIVA NO ATENDIMENTO EDUCACIONAL ESPECIALIZADO IMPLEMENTATION OF ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY IN SPECIAL EDUCATION IMPLEMENTACIÓN DE TECNOLOGÍA ASISTIVA EN LA ATENCIÓN EDUCATIVA ESPECIALIZADA The application of Assistive Technology (AT) resources in the school context is often directed toward students with disabilities in order to ensure better learning and participation conditions. The objective of this study was to present the process of implementing AT resources through a collaborative partnership with a teacher from a Specialized Educational Assistance Center (SEAC), specifically for students with physical disabilities. To achieve this, a semi-structured interview was conducted with the participant, along with the collection of information from institutional records regarding the clinical diagnosis and other relevant information about three students. Four AT resources were implemented based on the interview, the observation of the teacher’s practice at the SEAC, and the data collected about the students. title: FORMAÇÃO DOCENTE PARA PRÁTICAS INCLUSIVAS TEACHER EDUCATION FOR INCLUSIVE PRACTICES FORMACIÓN DOCENTE PARA PRÁCTICAS INCLUSIVAS
text_snippet: FORMAÇÃO DOCENTE PARA PRÁTICAS INCLUSIVAS TEACHER EDUCATION FOR INCLUSIVE PRACTICES FORMACIÓN DOCENTE PARA PRÁCTICAS INCLUSIVAS This article analyzes a continuing education experience developed with teachers of Specialized Educational Assistance (AEE), pedagogues, and administrators from the Municipal Network of Mandirituba/PR. The initiative was grounded in the principles of Universal Design (UD), Universal Design for Learning (UDL), and the use of Educational Assistive Technologies (EAT). Conducted by researchers from Federal University of Paraná (UFPR) in partnership with Laboratory of Educational Assistive Technologies (LabTAE), the program aimed to support professionals in identifying pedagogical barriers and redesigning instructional planning, fostering potentially inclusive and flexible practices. Using a qualitative and collaborative approach, the process integrated lectures, workshops, discussion circles, and technical visits, enabling the production of accessible materials and deepening teachers’ reflective practices. The results highlight advances in conceptual understanding of UDL, increased autonomy in the use of EATs, and the expansion of pedagogical strategies aimed at equity, demonstrating the potential of continuing education to strengthen educational practices responsive to diversity.

text_snippet: LAS TECNOLOGÍAS COMO SOPORTE EN EL DISEÑO UNIVERSAL PARA EL APRENDIZAJE 3.0 TECHNOLOGIES SUPPORTING UNIVERSAL DESIGN FOR LEARNING 3.0 AS TECNOLOGIAS COMO SUPORTE NO DESENHO UNIVERSAL PARA APRENDIZAGEM 3.0 Drawing on a theoretical framework based on specialized literature in educational technology and Universal Design for Learning (UDL), this article employs a qualitative methodology to present a theoretical-interpretative content analysis of the UDL Guidelines 3.0. The objective is to determine the presence of references to the use of technology or multimedia within this source. This analysis reveals eleven explicit allusions to technology utilization out of thirty-six references, spanning six of the nine guidelines within this instructional design framework presented in UDL 3.0, as well as its three core principles: engagement, representation, and action and expression. Furthermore, the analysis identifies direct connections between curricular proposal ideas for UDL and technological affordances. This study highlights that the primary advantage of technologies transcends their individual use, lying instead in their ease of combination with other media to meet students' specific needs, which aligns with the core philosophy of UDL to serve as a framework for all learners in the pursuit of an accessible and inclusive education. title: ENSINO DE DESENHO TEACHING DRAWING ENSEÑANZA DEL DIBUJO
text_snippet: ENSINO DE DESENHO TEACHING DRAWING ENSEÑANZA DEL DIBUJO Given the challenges faced by blind children and children with intellectual disabilities in learning to draw, this article presents two investigations grounded in childhood drawing and Visual Arts education that focus on this pedagogical practice. Both studies employed different types of lines, basic geometric shapes, and animal pictograms as mediation resources and teaching strategies, as proposed in the method presented in the book Pictographic Vocabulary for Inclusive Education. Data collection involved case studies, observation of activities, analysis of graphic records produced by the participants, and documentation of the process. The data were examined through a qualitative and interpretative approach, considering the progress observed throughout the activities developed. The results indicate that the schematization of forms promoted learning and enhanced the participants’ graphic expressiveness. It is concluded that such approaches contribute to the development of inclusive practices, with potential applications in the fields of Education, Arts, Accessibility, and Assistive Technology.

text_snippet: ENSINO DE CORES E DEFICIÊNCIA VISUAL COLOR TEACHING AND VISUAL IMPAIRMENT ENSEÑANZA DE COLORES Y DISCAPACIDAD VISUAL This article presents an expanded and revised version of the paper entitled “Exploring Textile Materials and Sensory Stimuli from the Artwork Valquíria Miss Dior for Inclusive Color Learning”, presented at the 5th Brazilian Congress on Assistive Technology (V CBTA). Based on the installation Valquíria Miss Dior (2013), by Joana Vasconcelos, the article discusses the potential of textile materials and multisensory stimuli as assistive technologies for teaching colors to people with visual impairments, within the contexts of design education and inclusive basic education. This qualitative and exploratory research combines a literature review on multisensoriality, Universal Design for Learning, and cultural accessibility with an interpretative analysis of the artwork, identifying sensory elements — such as textures, scales, aromas, and spatial organization — that can be pedagogically appropriated. title: MOUSE DE CABEÇA COMO RECURSO PEDAGÓGICO THE HEAD MOUSE AS A TEACHING TOOL RATÓN DE CABEZA COMO RECURSO PEDAGÓGICO
text_snippet: MOUSE DE CABEÇA COMO RECURSO PEDAGÓGICO THE HEAD MOUSE AS A TEACHING TOOL RATÓN DE CABEZA COMO RECURSO PEDAGÓGICO This work presents a technical training and accessibility-promotion experience through the development and use of a head mouse as a pedagogical tool in electronics workshops. The aim was to stimulate girls’ participation in technological fields while spreading knowledge about assistive technology and digital inclusion. The study adopted a qualitative and exploratory approach, developed in two stages: university students were trained in electronics and device assembly, and later acted as instructors in workshops with students from a public school. Results indicated the development of technical skills, improved understanding of assistive technology and increased awareness of accessibility. Participants reported greater confidence and interest in technology, reinforcing female leadership in a male-dominated field. The initiative strengthened the integration between teaching, research and outreach, promoting sustainable and low-cost solutions with replicability potential. The findings suggest that using an assistive device as a pedagogical tool contributes to both technical and citizenship education, fostering equitable access to technology and encouraging gender equity in STEM.

text_snippet: ACESSIBILIDADE E ALFABETIZAÇÃO ACCESSIBILITY AND LITERACY ACCESIBILIDAD Y ALFABETIZACIÓN Considering that a significant portion of the student population presents deficits in communication-related skills, this study aimed to develop a digital pedagogical resource to stimulate literacy precursor skills in children with Complex Communication Needs (CCN). The resource was constructed based on the principles of Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC), using pictographic symbols from the Aragonese Center of Augmentative and Alternative Communication (ARASAAC) and in accordance with ethical research principles. The research follows a qualitative and applied approach, consisting of implementing theoretical contributions from the fields of AAC, Assistive Technology (AT), and literacy in order to produce material intended to expand pedagogical possibilities within the educational context. As a result, a multiformat children's book was developed, featuring original illustrations and multiple accessibility resources, with a particular focus on stimulating phonological awareness through the use of rhymes. title: INFORMATIONAL SELF-DETERMINATION AND NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS AUTODETERMINACIÓN INFORMATIVA Y TRASTORNOS DEL NEURODESARROLLO AUTODETERMINAÇÃO INFORMACIONAL E TRANSTORNOS DO NEURODESENVOLVIMENTO
text_snippet: INFORMATIONAL SELF-DETERMINATION AND NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS AUTODETERMINACIÓN INFORMATIVA Y TRASTORNOS DEL NEURODESARROLLO AUTODETERMINAÇÃO INFORMACIONAL E TRANSTORNOS DO NEURODESENVOLVIMENTO This article explores the subject of access to data of people with neurodevelopmental disorders, focusing on the governance of health data generated during diagnostic and support processes. Current practices often limit individuals’ control over their data, despite the potential benefits for personalized care as well as for research. We address this matter by linking the concept of self-determination theory in Psychology and the legal concept of informational self-determination. We argue that bridging these concepts can enhance data governance, proposing practical solutions such as ethical data spaces. Our analysis integrates theoretical frameworks with case studies to advocate for policies that empower individuals while enabling responsible data sharing for research. By aligning technical standards with ethical and psychological insights, this work contributes to enlighten how data governance can foster better outcomes for neurodivergent people.

text_snippet: ACESSIBILIDADE NA PRODUÇÃO CIENTÍFICA ACCESSIBILITY IN SCIENTIFIC PRODUCTION ACCESIBILIDAD EN LA PRODUCCIÓN CIENTÍFICA Accessibility is understood as a process of practical action aimed at identifying and removing barriers in order to enable the effective participation of individuals in different spheres of social life, particularly in activities inherent to the academic career. Accordingly, this study aimed to explore the role of Accessibility and Assistive Technology (AT) in access to knowledge production, based on an account of my academic trajectory as a researcher with visual impairment. This is an autobiographical study developed through the construction of an inventory of personal experiences, focusing on the different ways in which barriers to access to scientific knowledge were imposed throughout my schooling, academic training, and professional practice, as well as on the strategies developed to overcome them. The reflections made it possible to identify that, initially, access to scientific production was enabled through the use of personal strategies and devices designed to make materials accessible. title: ORIENTAÇÃO ACADÊMICA E A BAIXA VISÃO ACADEMIC SUPERVISION AND LOW VISION ORIENTACIÓN ACADÉMICA Y LA BAJA VISIÓN
text_snippet: ORIENTAÇÃO ACADÊMICA E A BAIXA VISÃO ACADEMIC SUPERVISION AND LOW VISION ORIENTACIÓN ACADÉMICA Y LA BAJA VISIÓN This narrative explores the challenges and possibilities of academic supervision involving students with low vison in graduate programs. Drawing on the lived experiences of a low vision student, a low vision supervisor, and a sighted supervisor in a professional master’s program at an institution specialized in visual impairment, the study adopts a qualitative approach, combining personal narratives with contributions of the Brazilian legislation and the literature on inclusive education. The findings reveal multiple barriers faced by students with visual impairments, including inaccessible institutional infrastructure, technological and informational obstacles, and attitudinal challenges within the academic community. The role of the supervisor emerges, not only in guiding scientific production but also in advocating for accessible materials, adjusting timelines, and fostering an environment of empathy and trust. The study highlights innovative pedagogical practices, such as remote meetings to facilitate reading and writing, the use of assistive technologies, and personalized planning that respects each student's pace and needs. title: ACESSIBILIDADE EM DOCUMENTOS DIGITAIS PARA INCLUSÃO NO ACESSO AO CONHECIMENTO CIENTÍFICO ACCESSIBILITY IN DIGITAL DOCUMENTS FOR INCLUSION IN ACCESS TO SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE ACCESIBILIDAD EN DOCUMENTOS DIGITALES PARA LA INCLUSIÓN EN EL ACCESO AL CONOCIMIENTO CIENTÍFICO
text_snippet: ACESSIBILIDADE EM DOCUMENTOS DIGITAIS PARA INCLUSÃO NO ACESSO AO CONHECIMENTO CIENTÍFICO ACCESSIBILITY IN DIGITAL DOCUMENTS FOR INCLUSION IN ACCESS TO SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE ACCESIBILIDAD EN DOCUMENTOS DIGITALES PARA LA INCLUSIÓN EN EL ACCESO AL CONOCIMIENTO CIENTÍFICO this paper presents a set of guidelines for producing accessible digital documents that support people with disabilities (visual, auditory, physical, and intellectual) and individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), grounded in the understanding that accessibility in digital documents is a prerequisite for ensuring access to rights, particularly the human right to information and education. The guidelines were compiled and organized based on bibliographic and documentary research, as well as the authors’ experience in educational and training activities. They encompass a range of document types, including calls for applications to graduate programs, theses, dissertations, and undergraduate final projects, produced as text-based documents and made available in .doc files (compatible with Microsoft Word, LibreOffice, and other word processors) and in the .pdf format (Portable Document Format), which is supported by a wide variety of document readers. Beyond its conceptual contribution, this paper also aims to support the implementation of inclusive praxis by promoting equitable access to scientific knowledge.

text_snippet: APRESENTAÇÃO Presentation Presentación This proposal is situated within a global context in which individuals with visual, hearing, physical, intellectual, deafblind, or multiple disabilities—whether or not they present with Autism Spectrum Disorder—as well as older adults, have increasingly entered and participated in academic-scientific communities. Consequently, a need has emerged for investigations regarding accessibility in the production and dissemination of scientific knowledge. This is because studies have indicated that this population still faces significant attitudinal, technological, ergonomic, informational, and communicational barriers in teaching, research, extension, and management activities, in both in-person and distance modalities. In this regard, this dossier gathers studies addressing this theme, which aligns with international frameworks such as the 2006 Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, the 2013 Marrakesh Treaty, the 2015 Agenda 2030 for Sustainable Development, and the 2021 UNESCO Recommendation on Open Science, as well as the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines and the Brazilian Standards (NBRs) issued by the Brazilian Association of Technical Standards – ABNT NBR 17225, b

text_snippet: AUDIODESCRIÇÃO POÉTICA POETIC AUDIODESCRIPTION AUDIODESCRIPCIÓN POÉTICA This article seeks to systematize the practice of Poetic Audio Description, an aesthetic accessibility resource already in use within the field of the arts. Based on a literature review on the subject and on the authorship’s experiences and research, it proposes a concept, foundations, and guidelines for Poetic Audio Description, presenting procedures and examples for its implementation. It is grounded in the understanding that Audio Description constitutes a work of intersemiotic translation and recreation and, within the context of the arts, a practice that should be supported by the principles and standards of traditional Audio Description, by the poetics of the work to be translated, by the specificities of artistic languages, and by the linguistic-expressive resources of poetic language. This requires translational choices that enable a singular, aesthetic, transformative, and creative experience, while preserving the aesthetic enjoyment intrinsic to the work in dialogue with the poetics that constitutes it. title: INTERAÇÃO HUMANO-COMPUTADOR NA PRODUÇÃO E DIFUSÃO DO CONHECIMENTO CIENTÍFICO COM ACESSIBILIDADE HUMAN-COMPUTER INTERACTION IN THE PRODUCTION AND DISSEMINATION OF SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE WITH ACCESSIBILITY Interacción persona-computadora en la producción y difusión de conocimiento científico con accesibilidad
text_snippet: INTERAÇÃO HUMANO-COMPUTADOR NA PRODUÇÃO E DIFUSÃO DO CONHECIMENTO CIENTÍFICO COM ACESSIBILIDADE HUMAN-COMPUTER INTERACTION IN THE PRODUCTION AND DISSEMINATION OF SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE WITH ACCESSIBILITY Interacción persona-computadora en la producción y difusión de conocimiento científico con accesibilidad This article examines the technical-scientific framework of the Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) field as a support for digital inclusion initiatives in the processes of scientific knowledge production and dissemination. In this context, it discusses how HCI methods help identify accessibility and usability issues, as well as proposed solutions. The discussion involves the various roles played by users, especially those with visual impairments, though not limited to them — such as authors, readers, or reviewers — and the barriers/problems they face when using systems and software. Additionally, the study addresses issues related to scientific content itself, such as charts, images, and tables, considering the specificities of different fields of knowledge. The work contributes to guiding practices, tools, and editorial policies that promote accessibility. It also reinforces the importance of HCI in building a more inclusive and equitable scientific environment.

title: ACESSIBILIDADE EM LIVROS DIGITAIS ACADÊMICOS ACCESSIBILITY IN ACADEMIC DIGITAL BOOKS ACCESIBILIDAD EN LIBROS DIGITALES ACADÉMICOS
text_snippet: ACESSIBILIDADE EM LIVROS DIGITAIS ACADÊMICOS ACCESSIBILITY IN ACADEMIC DIGITAL BOOKS ACCESIBILIDAD EN LIBROS DIGITALES ACADÉMICOS SciELO Books is a collection that, since its inception, has aimed to expand access, impact and visibility of scientific publications in digital format, adopting editorial practices aligned with international guidelines. In recent years, scientific publishers have begun to pay attention to the importance of implementing accessibility policies in their publications in order to facilitate access to works by blind people, those with visual impairments or other reading difficulties. In this context, in 2024, SciELO Books established a partnership with Editora UEMG to produce 100% accessible digital books, expanding the guidelines and practices already consolidated in the collection. This article presents practical aspects of the production of accessible digital books and describes the implementation process carried out, in a pioneering manner, by SciELO Books and Editora UEMG. It also seeks to offer support to publishers interested in adopting accessibility practices in their publications.

title: ACESSIBILIDADE, DIREITOS HUMANOS E DEMOCRACIA NA REVISTA BRASILEIRA DE EDUCAÇÃO ESPECIAL ACCESSIBILITY, HUMAN RIGHTS AND DEMOCRACY IN THE REVISTA BRASILEIRA DE EDUCAÇÃO ESPECIAL ACCESIBILIDAD, DERECHOS HUMANOS Y DEMOCRACIA EN LA REVISTA BRASILEIRA DE EDUCAÇÃO ESPECIAL
text_snippet: ACESSIBILIDADE, DIREITOS HUMANOS E DEMOCRACIA NA REVISTA BRASILEIRA DE EDUCAÇÃO ESPECIAL ACCESSIBILITY, HUMAN RIGHTS AND DEMOCRACY IN THE REVISTA BRASILEIRA DE EDUCAÇÃO ESPECIAL ACCESIBILIDAD, DERECHOS HUMANOS Y DEMOCRACIA EN LA REVISTA BRASILEIRA DE EDUCAÇÃO ESPECIAL This article addresses the practices of scientific knowledge production and dissemination, from an accessibility perspective, developed by the Revista Brasileira de Educação Especial (RBEE). We understand that education and knowledge production are public goods and, therefore, should be made available to all. Thus, accessibility constitutes a political and ethical concept linked to the field of human rights and democracy. From this perspective, the RBEE, in partnership with the Grupo de Trabalho Interdisciplinar para a Acessibilidade da Rede SciELO, has developed initiatives to promote accessibility in the production and dissemination of articles: improving editorial standards, with guidelines for authors on accessibility; meetings with professionals responsible for journal layout; and the production of alternative texts for describing images used in articles, among others. We hope that the practices described will provide support for other journals in implementing initiatives aimed at expanding informational and communicational accessibility.

title: INCLUSIVE SOLUTIONS SOLUCIONES INCLUSIVAS SOLUÇÕES INCLUSIVAS
text_snippet: INCLUSIVE SOLUTIONS SOLUCIONES INCLUSIVAS SOLUÇÕES INCLUSIVAS This paper delves into the various inclusion strategies aimed at enhancing students’ scientific writing proficiency, particularly in the context of dissertations and theses. It investigates the impact of compensatory and enabling measures — such as digital tools, accommodations, and alternative methods — on cognitive processes inherent to academic writing. These processes encompass memory, attention, executive functions, and language processing. The article critically examines how assistive technologies and systematic adjustments mitigate cognitive load, foster higher-order thinking, and ultimately enhance the clarity and coherence of students ‘written work, thus promoting an inclusive academic environment for students with diverse learning needs.

This was an exploratory qualitative study involving six family members of children aged 3 to 6 years with spastic quadriplegic CP, ranging from Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) levels I to IV. Data collection was conducted through semi-structured interviews based on the concepts of the Family of Constructs related to Participation and on the environmental factors described in the International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health. Data analysis was performed using thematic content analysis. Four categories were formulated: favorite play activities; child's attendance in activities; child's engagement in activities; and environmental factors influencing participation. School attendance facilitated the diverse offering of activities, regardless of the level of motor function or type of CP. I

title: “TEM QUE APOSTAR A TODO TEMPO” YOU HAVE TO BET ALL THE TIME Tienes que apostar todo el tiempo
text_snippet: “TEM QUE APOSTAR A TODO TEMPO” YOU HAVE TO BET ALL THE TIME Tienes que apostar todo el tiempo The aim is to understand educational practices with autistic children and discuss barriers and facilitators at school through interviews with a leading teacher and a support assistant intern who worked in partnership in the schooling of an autistic child enrolled in elementary school. This is a qualitative, exploratory study that analyzed the content of fully transcribed semi-structured interviews. The results indicate that the attitudes of empathy, collaboration, creativity, listening, interest, search, investigation and elaboration of learning hypotheses between the teacher and intern favored adaptations in teaching that provided conditions conducive to the development and learning of autistic children, configuring the school as a potential storehouse of innovative and inclusive pedagogical practices.

The research was conducted with two families from Landri Sales/PI, using an ethnographic and qualitative approach that included semi-structured interviews, participant observation, and artifact collection. The study is grounded in New Literacy Studies and Multiliteracies. Findings indicate that literacy practices influence participants' identities, shaped by discourses on disability found in educational and religious contexts. These practices reflect values such as rights, care, and charity, helping family members mediate the participation of individuals with disabilities in various activities. Additionally, participants engage in informal literacy practices, especially in virtual environments, which provide significant spaces for personal expression. Thus, identities in literacy practices

title: A GLOBALIZAÇÃO E A INCLUSÃO ESCOLAR GLOBALIZATION AND SCHOOL INCLUSION GLOBALIZACIÓN E INCLUSIÓN ESCOLAR
text_snippet: A GLOBALIZAÇÃO E A INCLUSÃO ESCOLAR GLOBALIZATION AND SCHOOL INCLUSION GLOBALIZACIÓN E INCLUSIÓN ESCOLAR In all its definitions, education reflects historical contradictions that need to be reflected upon, namely: how to educate the deaf, the blind, the intellectually disabled and the autistic in common spaces? Based on this premise, the modernity project would be complete when all individuals had a place in school. Taking the theoretical-methodological perspective of bibliographic and documentary research with a critical analysis approach, this work aimed to reflect on the medical discourse and its implications for the inclusive processes present in the school context, primarily related to the autistic student, within the scope of a medical-clinical model, whose materiality impacts the construction of inclusive pedagogical practices. As a result, we point out that the process of inclusion of people with autism requires greater reflection regarding the current pedagogical debate, as well as the understanding of this practice based on a formative model that can extrapolate an eminently clinical conception. text_snippet: MODELOS DE COMPREENSÃO DA DEFICIÊNCIA: CONCEPÇÕES E REFLEXÕES MODELS OF UNDERSTANDING DISABILITY: CONCEPTIONS AND REFLECTIONS MODELOS DE COMPRENSIÓN DE LA DISCAPACIDAD: CONCEPTOS Y REFLEXIONES This text is a theoretical essay on the models used to analyze disability. These models are historical and cultural constructions that shape conceptions of bodies and intellects, affecting the way subjects are read, treated and understood in society, which in turn affects their development and autonomy. The text aims to present three predominant models of analysis in the literature on disability and how they continue to be perpetuated today: the charity model, the biomedical model and the social model of disability. The charity model arises from religious beliefs and is based on welfare practices that perceive people with disabilities as subjects worthy of pity. The biomedical model, in turn, has its origins in scientific knowledge and seeks to correct, cure and punish the impairment in order to achieve an imposed normality. And finally, the social model of disability understands disability not as the consequence of an injury, but as the result of a collective situation of institutionalized discrimination, organized culturally in contemporary times, in a relational way. The aim of this article is to contextualize part of the scenario of scientific knowledge production about the applications, purposes and development of Augmentative and Alternative Communication. It is an integrative review of articles published in journals indexed in different databases in Brazil and Portugal. Based on the application of previously established inclusion and exclusion criteria, 23 studies, including articles and dissertations, were selected to constitute the corpus of analysis. The results show that the studies analyzed recognize and consider the potential of Augmentative and Alternative Communication in communicative acts and social interactions between people with communication difficulties and their interlocutors. Therefore, this research sought to reflect on the challenges of this process, specifically in the literacy cycle. To this end, the research included observation of meetings, document analysis, semi-structured interviews and focus group interviews with teachers. The data were analyzed using the hermeneutic-dialectic conception. Based on the results found, we understand that, despite the difficulties generated by the pandemic, IBC was structured and trained teachers, guardians and students before remote teaching began, which was fundamental for the development of accessible classes. Despite this, we conclude that face-to-face teaching is essential for these students who have touch as one of the main senses for collecting information and constructing learning. Due to the lack of knowledge about all forms of transmission of Covid-19, the Ministry of Health has guided the population, in addition to individual prophylaxis actions (hand hygiene and use of masks), isolation and social distancing, this has also included the closure of schools. Thus, this article aimed to analyze the access conditions of students with Autism Spectrum Disorder to emergency remote education, enrolled in a public school in the outskirts of the city. The research was based on the theoretical-methodological assumptions of historical-cultural theory, with emphasis on the dialectical relationship between the environment and experience/perezhivanie, in the process of human development and as the unit of analysis in investigative processes. Thus, acting as a class teacher and researcher, we based our work on the records of pedagogical activities and contact with families via the WhatsApp application and the field diary. title: TECNOLOGIA ASSISTIVA E ACESSIBILIDADE ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY AND ACCESSIBILITY TECNOLOGÍA DE ASISTENCIA Y ACCESIBILIDAD
text_snippet: TECNOLOGIA ASSISTIVA E ACESSIBILIDADE ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY AND ACCESSIBILITY TECNOLOGÍA DE ASISTENCIA Y ACCESIBILIDAD Brazilian public policies of the 21st century, in line with global guidelines, advocate for the enrollment of students with disabilities in regular educational institutions and for these institutions to provide appropriate accessibility conditions, considering their various dimensions: architectural, pedagogical, methodological, pedagogical, informational, communicational, instrumental, programmatic, attitudinal, and digital. Faced with this challenge, this work aims to present, discuss, and reflect on actions in the school environment to promote accessibility in its multiple dimensions, in order to preserve and guarantee the learning rights of students with Visual Impairments (VI). The research is qualitative in nature and is based on the principles of collaborative action research, supported by literature and documentary reviews that address the topic of accessibility, and was conducted in a Federal Education network institution. As results, a series of educational and Assistive Technology resources indispensable to the education of students with VI are presented, as well as strategies and guidelines for implementing these resources in practice.

This work, with a qualitative and exploratory, portrays an experience report on the use of a multisensory material developed for teaching organic functions, with a focus on teaching people with visual impairments. The educational product developed in this work consists of multisensory teaching material that allows exploration through more than one sensory pathway, such as hearing, touch, taste, taste and vision. Five blind students and one student with low vision were invited to participate in this study, who explored the educational product developed to study the proposed phenomenon. During the exploration of the product, data were collected through photographs and observations noted in a field diary. title: MODOS DE ELABORAÇÃO DE RECURSOS DIDÁTICOS PARA ALUNOS COM TRANSTORNO DO ESPECTRO AUTISTA (TEA) METHODS OF PREPARING TEACHING RESOURCES FOR STUDENTS WITH AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER MÉTODOS DE DESARROLLO DE RECURSOS DIDÁCTICOS PARA ESTUDIANTES CON TRASTORNO DEL ESPECTRO AUTISTA

It presents strategies for developing these resources, including guidelines for their selection and use, based on guidelines from specialized professionals. The importance of knowing the individual needs of students with ASD is highlighted to create adapted and personalized resources. Resources such as visual materials, assistive technologies and sensory activities are essential to cater to different learning styles. Implementing these resources is crucial to promoting inclusion and providing more learning and development opportunities for all students. The study also explores the period and essential elements for the development of these resources, highlighting the importance of active participation in this process. It is concluded that the adaptation and personalization of resources, combined with the guidance of specialized professionals, are fundamental to guarantee their effectiveness and relevance in the educational context of students with Autism

title: Diálogos sobre Educação, Inclusão e Escola Dialogues on Education, Inclusion and School Diálogos sobre Educación, Inclusión y Escuela
text_snippet: Diálogos sobre Educação, Inclusão e Escola Dialogues on Education, Inclusion and School Diálogos sobre Educación, Inclusión y Escuela Volume twelve, number four of the Journal of Dialogues and Perspectives in Special Education (RDPEE) for 2025, consists of 15 articles presenting works that interrelate education, inclusion, and school, dialogically and in different national and international contexts. This issue presents studies on the Special Education population, as well as all the actors involved in their human development process, mediated by education, presenting the school as a platform for dialogue within Brazilian and Portuguese society regarding inclusion. Research reports, experience reports, and systematic and bibliographic reviews are presented. We hope that this issue will contribute to academic studies, but above all, to the training of teachers, researchers, and civil society in advancing topics that promote the interrelationship between education, inclusion, and school.

Nine Biology teachers from municipal schools located in Abaetetuba, state of Pará, in the northern region of Brazil, selected from a non-random convenience sample, took part in the study. The data collection instruments used were a questionnaire to characterize the participants and a structured individual interview. A word cloud was chosen, using the IRaMuTeQ software. The main results found were related to the lack of specific training to work with Special and Inclusive Education, which reflected in adaptations of materials and activities, as well as a lack of ability to work with deaf students. This study critically examines the diagnostic evaluation processes, including screening instruments and treatment methods employed in a specialized autism clinic in northern Brazil. Using a qualitative documentary approach, the research details the workflow and therapeutic indications of the Mundo Autista School Clinic (CEMA), a public, non-profit institution supported by the Municipal Government of Araguaína (TO) in 2021. Findings indicate that the diagnostic and treatment procedures for individuals with ASD are centered on a multidisciplinary intervention approach, leading to substantial improvements in quality of life while respecting the individual's developmental level and unique characteristics. title: INCLUSÃO ESCOLAR DE ESTUDANTES COM TRANSTORNO DO ESPECTRO AUTISTA (TEA) E O PAPEL DOS AUXILIARES DE SERVIÇOS EDUCACIONAIS NA REDE MUNICIPAL DE PIRIPIRI-PI SCHOOL INCLUSION OF STUDENTS WITH AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER (ASD) AND THE ROLE OF EDUCATIONAL SUPPORT STAFF IN THE MUNICIPAL NETWORK OF PIRIPIRI-PI INCLUSIÓN ESCOLAR DE ESTUDIANTES CON TRASTORNO DEL ESPECTRO AUTISTA (TEA) Y EL PAPEL DEL PERSONAL DE APOYO EDUCATIVO EN LA RED MUNICIPAL DE PIRIPIRI-PI

Adopting a qualitative approach, the research involved the participation of one administrator from the Municipal Department of Education (SEDUC) of Piripiri-PI; two staff members from the Department of Educational Assistance (DAE) of SEDUC; one school principal; one school coordinator; one mainstream classroom teacher; and one educational support staff member working in the municipal network of Piripiri-PI. Data collection was carried out through semi-structured interviews, which enabled reflections on how the inclusion of students with ASD takes place in this context. text_snippet: EFEITOS DAS POLÍTICAS DE EDUCAÇÃO INCLUSIVA NOS CURSOS DE LICENCIATURA EM EDUCAÇÃO DO CAMPO - CIÊNCIAS DA NATUREZA (RS) EFFECTS OF INCLUSIVE EDUCATION POLICIES ON UNDERGRADUATE COURSES IN RURAL EDUCATION - NATURAL SCIENCES (RS) This article aims to analyze the effects of Inclusive Education policies on undergraduate courses in Rural Education, which aim to train teachers to work in basic education in the area of ​​Natural Sciences. This is part of a research project that seeks to map Inclusive Education policies and their implications in the curricula of two courses offered by the Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS) – one of them on the Central Campus, in Porto Alegre, and the other one in the coastal region, in the city of Tramandaí. The methodology follows a post-structuralist approach, inspired by Foucault, with the use of concepts such as discourse and governmentality. The method of documentary analysis was adopted, considering the Inclusive Education policies and the Pedagogical Projects of the Courses (PPCs) in order to understand how work with the differences of the subjects is proposed in the courses, regarding their curricular organization. The results have shown that the main inclusive policies have an impact on the courses and are translated into knowledge that comprises the context of Special Education, diversity and inclusion. text_snippet: POLÍTICAS DE INCLUSÃO INCLUSION POLICIES POLÍTICAS DE INCLUSIÓN The process of inclusion in education has revealed challenging scenarios for the target audience of special education.
